Voatdev

Last week in /v/voatdev there were repeat reports about previously known bugs, like having one's username visually replaced with someone else's, getting logged out by clicking on /v/all/top, and the user "Follow" button not being clickable. There was one point of note, however; a post presenting the idea that every user have a uniquely tailored front page in terms of upvotes shown, where users can choose to remove the upvotes given from certain users from the posts they see. However, not only would such a feature be resource intensive to the point of being completely infeasible, but I don't think that kind of difference betweens what users see would be desirable. It is one thing to choose to not see certain posts that others may see, but to choose to see one post differently than others see it would be a terrible cause of confusion, in my opinion anyway. Still, an interesting idea.

VoatStatistics

Posts per day for last week: Last week Thursday had the most submissions site-wide, at 2,207, with the total number of submissions throughout the week numbering 14,169. It was Saturday, however, that had the most comments of the week, at 18,647, with 124,042 comments site-wide all week long.

Most commented posts for last week: The most commented post last week was one announcing the death of George H. W. Bush, the 41st president of the United States of America. Being a controversial figure, and a momentous figure, his death is certainly something to spark discussion.

Most controversial posts last week: Amazingly, a picture of a puppy with flowers was the most controversial post last week. This is due to the controversy that has been surrounding /v/aww in general for about two weeks now (almost every controversial post this week was from /v/aww). Some people have been posting gore to /v/aww (which would not be an issue if the moderators were active and removing said content -- which will be rectifiable once the Votes feature, and therefore subverse transfer capability, launches), and others have been posting lots of actual /v/aww-worthy content in order to "counter-act" the gore. Interestingly, many goats have become annoyed at the constant presence of the actual /v/aww content on their front pages, and have taken to downvoting it. However, I doubt that the downvotes are purely organic; the example above has almost equal downvotes to upvotes, suggesting possible manipulation one way or another.

While I will say that "counter-acting" the gore seems unnecessary, since the gore gets downvoted reliably and never makes it to the front page, I still don't think downvoting content one does not want to see is reasonable -- the proper course of action would be to remove that subverse from one's front page, and let those who want to see such content enjoy it. This is possible, as I demonstrated here, but many seem reluctant to go to the effort necessary to properly tailor their front pages, and so they just downvote the default content they do not want to see, but which they could hide entirely if they just unsubscribed from the subverse (either by no longer subscribing to the /s/Default set, or by directly unsubscribing from the subverse if they are subscribed). But again, I doubt all of these downvotes are from ordinary users, and suspect that some of it, if not all, many be artificial.
